title: Rama and Sita
captions: When the great bow broke, King Janaka's heart filled with joy. “I have seen Rama's strength with my own eyes,” he said. “My promise is kept. My dear daughter Sita will marry Rama.”
“Great sage, with your permission, my messengers will go to Ayodhya in swift chariots to invite King Dasharatha,” said Janaka. Vishvamitra agreed, and the messengers raced away.
After three nights on the road, the tired messengers reached Ayodhya. They bowed to King Dasharatha and said, “Your son Rama has broken Lord Shiva's bow! King Janaka wishes Sita to marry him.”
Dasharatha was filled with joy. He turned to his guru Vasishtha, the sage Vamadeva and his ministers. “If this pleases you, let us go to Mithila,” he said. “Very good!” they all replied.
The very next morning, Dasharatha set out with his army and many gifts. The sages went ahead of him on the road. After four days of travel, they reached Mithila.
King Janaka came out joyfully to welcome Dasharatha. “By good fortune you have come, great king,” he said. “When my yajna is complete, let the wedding take place.”
Then Rama and Lakshmana came with Vishvamitra and bowed at their father's feet. Dasharatha was overjoyed to see his sons again, and everyone rested happily that night.
story: When the great bow broke, King Janaka's heart filled with joy. He had seen Rama's strength with his own eyes, and his promise was kept. His dear daughter Sita would marry Rama.

With Vishvamitra's permission, Janaka sent messengers to Ayodhya in swift chariots to invite King Dasharatha. After three nights on the road, the tired messengers reached Ayodhya, bowed to the king and gave him the wonderful news.

Dasharatha was filled with joy, but he did not rush off on his own. He turned to his guru Vasishtha, the sage Vamadeva and his ministers and asked what they thought. They all agreed that it was very good news.

The very next morning, Dasharatha set out with his army and many gifts, and the sages travelled ahead of him on the road. After four days they reached Mithila, where King Janaka came out joyfully to welcome them. Janaka asked that the wedding take place once his yajna was complete.
Then Rama and Lakshmana came with Vishvamitra and bowed at their father's feet. Dasharatha was overjoyed to see his sons again after their long adventure, and everyone rested happily that night.
lesson: When the happy news came, King Dasharatha did not rush off on his own. He first asked his guru Vasishtha and the elders, and on the road he let the sages go in front of him. King Janaka, too, planned the wedding for after his sacred yajna was complete. In our tradition, Mangala means a good and blessed beginning, and our elders teach that every happy new start goes best with the blessings of God and of those who love us.
lesson_long: Mangala means good, blessed and auspicious. A mangala beginning is a start made with care and with blessings.

When the happy news came, King Dasharatha first asked his guru and the elders. On the road, he let the sages go ahead of him. King Janaka, too, planned the wedding for after his sacred yajna. Both kings wanted this new beginning to start the right way.
Our elders teach that every happy new start goes best with the blessings of God and of those who love us.
tradition: Before starting anything new, many Hindu families first pray to Lord Ganesha, who removes obstacles. Families also ask a priest to choose a muhurtham, a good time, for weddings, housewarmings and other big events.

The word mangala appears in many happy places. The sacred thread a bride wears in many communities is called the mangalsutra, and the joyful music played at South Indian weddings is called mangala vadyam.
words: a good time chosen for an important event
the sacred thread worn by a bride
a respected sage in King Dasharatha's court
question: Before you start something new and important, whose blessings would you like to ask for?
questions: Before you start something new and important, whose blessings would you like to ask for?
Why did King Dasharatha ask his guru before going to Mithila?
What does our family do to start a new year, a new school term or a new home?
card_lesson: King Dasharatha first asked his guru and the elders, then set out for Mithila with the sages in front. Mangala means starting something new with blessings.
